title: Psalm 122: Pray for the Peace of Jerusalem
summary: A pilgrim remembers the joy of being invited to go up to the house of the LORD and now stands inside Jerusalem's gates. He praises the city as the place where Israel's tribes gather to give thanks and where the thrones of David's house give justice, then calls for prayer for Jerusalem's peace and commits himself to seek its good for the sake of his people and of God's house.

from.text: Psalm 120 opens the Songs of Ascents, a collection of fifteen short psalms (120 to 134) that each carry the heading

line: A pilgrim glad to be invited to the house of the LORD stands inside Jerusalem's gates and calls for prayer for its peace.
guide: Ask whether worship with God's people is something you are glad to go to, who invited you, and whom you might invite. Pray for the peace of Jerusalem and everyone who lives there, and for your own town and the people hardest to love; prayer for peace leads to work for peace.

care.text: Verse 6 is often quoted today in arguments about the modern city and the modern state. These notes make no claim about any modern state, government, border or conflict, and nothing here is said against any people who live in that land. In its own setting the psalm is a pilgrim's prayer for the city of the temple. Christians apply it in different ways: some pray for the city of Jerusalem itself and all who live there; others read it chiefly of the heavenly Jerusalem and God's people everywhere; many hold both. Whatever a reader draws from it, the psalm asks for shalom, which includes justice and the good of neighbours. It is a prayer anyone may pray for a city and its people. Its words cannot be used to bless hatred or harm.

stanzas.title: Glad at the call to go up; standing in the gates
Jerusalem: where the tribes give thanks and justice sits
A call to pray for the city's peace
Seeking the city's good for others' sake

verses.t: A song of ascents. Of David. I was glad when they said to me, “Let us go to the house of the LORD.”
Our feet are standing in your gates, O Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is built up as a city united together,
where the tribes go up, the tribes of the LORD, as a testimony for Israel, to give thanks to the name of the LORD.
For there the thrones of judgment stand, the thrones of the house of David.
Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: “May those who love you prosper.
May there be peace within your walls, and prosperity inside your fortresses.”
For the sake of my brothers and friends, I will say, “Peace be within you.”
For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I will seek your prosperity.
